stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria on a complex Next.js preview-routing story involving CMS draft integration and protected-page limitations. openspec must elaborate AC and add technical depth on preview-mode routing, draft API integration, and protected-content constraints. speckit must then harden for security (draft exposure, auth on protected pages, preview-token handling) and add testability/edge-case criteria. Both agents warranted due to complexity and security sensitivity.

agentContributions.notes: Novel feature — no live preview capability exists. ContentstackContext is the central attachment point: it holds all CMS content (header, footer, page, directories) consumed by every Contentstack component via useContent. Live Preview's onEntryChange must plug into this context's provider to re-render with draft data. The useContent hook (src/hooks/useContent.ts) is the consumption layer that will need to respond to preview-driven updates. No provider component was found in search results, so it likely lives in an app-layout file not yet examined; the context itself is the stable anchor.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with valuable architectural notes. I examined the actual codebase to write testable criteria. Key findings: (1) ContentstackContext is a simple createContext with fields for header, footer, page, directories — live preview must update this context value to propagate draft data. (2) useContent hook consumes the context and exposes getContentByKey; it re-renders when the context value changes, so updating the context is sufficient. (3) No existing live preview code exists anywhere in the codebase. (4) No ContentstackContext.Provider was found in search results — it likely lives in an app-layout file. (5) IContentstackPage includes _content_type_uid and uid fields needed for Contentstack entry correlation. (6) Mock files show _metadata.uid on components — preserved UIDs are needed for CMS-to-component mapping. AC-1 through AC-6 cover the happy path (init, draft rendering, context propagation, content types). AC-7 covers the stated protected-page limitation. AC-8 and AC-9 cover error/connection resilience. AC-10 covers production performance non-regression. AC-11 and AC-12 cover navigation behaviors. AC-13 covers multi-codeline build compatibility (a real concern given the .ts vs .tsx and case differences noted in resolved files). AC-14 covers UID preservation for CMS mapping. AC-15 covers rapid-event handling to prevent UI jitter.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes:
Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. openspec established the architectural understanding: ContentstackContext as the central attachment point holding all CMS content, useContent as the consumption layer feeding every Contentstack component, and confirmed no existing live-preview code anywhere in the codebase. speckit then authored 7 detailed verification criteria covering the happy path (init, draft rendering, context propagation), regression baseline (published content unchanged), protected-page limitation handling, and configuration correctness. The criteria describe observable outcomes — rendered page showing draft vs published content, no browser reload, no visual/functional regression — alongside internal mechanism references that the guardVocabulary blacklist correctly flags.

MANIFEST EVIDENCE: All 5 declared paths EXIST in the upexpress codeline (confirmed by filesystem stat). The perCodeline analysis shows 2 mock files unresolved in gotransit and metrolinx codelines, but speckit's AC-13 explicitly addresses cross-codeline build compatibility as a real concern given the .ts vs .tsx and case differences. No missing_manifest_path flag needed for the working codeline.

PLAN ALIGNMENT: The detective planned to trace useContent to find the Contentstack SDK client config and look for Next.js preview API routes. The final fixSiteAnalysis landed on ContentstackContext instead. This is a justified deviation: the fixSiteAnalysis explains the pivot — 'useContent hook and getValue utility need no changes — they already read from this context generically' and 'Live preview must plug into this context — either by extending its provider to accept preview/draft data.' The detective traced useContent (a plan term) and found it leads to ContentstackContext (the finding term) as the actual injection point. The fix also references Next.js API routes and server-side fetching, connecting back to plan terms. The reasoning chain is stated and coherent.

One open question: the fixSiteAnalysis prescribes creating a Next.js /api/preview route and modifying server-side fetching (getServerSideProps/getStaticProps), but no such files appear in the declared set. This is an ordinary open question a competent writer resolves by creating new files — not a blocking defect, as the declared files (ContentstackContext, useContent, page.ts, mock files) are the correct attachment points for the core change.
